subject: Staging fleet: regional sizing and burst policy tradeoffs for HeliumHealth
messages:
From: Alicia Vega <alicia.vega@heliumhealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Bowers <tom.bowers@heliumhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Initial ask — staging region and burst behavior for dedicated pool

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — excited to move forward with Redwood Dedicated for our inference pipelines. Before we lock a timeline, we need to agree on two things for staging:

- Which region(s) you recommend for our staging pool (we expect most traffic from west US, some east coast dev tests).
- A sensible burst/autoscale policy for the first 90 days (we want cost control but need headroom for unpredictable nightly inference batches).

Quick context: our model is a 30B transformer, average seq length ~512 for batched jobs, and we start with an expected sustained 6 qps but burst up to ~60 qps during nightly re-runs. We prefer to avoid frequent model fallbacks.

Can you confirm next steps and any info you need from our side? If possible, copy your internal ops lead so we can align on provisioning windows.

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Vega
Head of ML Ops, HeliumHealth

Attachments: helhealth-inference-profile.csv (referenced)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Vega <alicia.vega@heliumhealth.com>
Cc: Tom Bowers <tom.bowers@heliumhealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 13:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Initial ask — staging region and burst behavior for dedicated pool

Hi Alicia — great talking earlier. Short answer up front: US-West (closest to your production) for staging with a small east coast warm standby, and a staged burst policy (baseline min capacity + warm reserve + short-duration burst cap). Proposed plan and asks below.

Proposed staging plan (90-day ramp):
- Region: primary us-west-2 for staging compute (latency/cost sweet spot for your traffic). Secondary warm standby in us-east-1 (single AZ) for failover testing.
- Initial pool sizing: reserve 8 vGPUs (NVIDIA A100x with quantized 16-bit path) — expected to cover sustained 6 qps with 2x headroom.
- Autoscale policy: min=2 nodes, target steady=8 nodes, max=24 nodes. Add a warm reserve of 4 nodes (pre-warmed model instances) for <30s cold-starts. Burst window = short (<=10 minutes) with token-based throttles to protect cost.
- Fallbacks: automatic model variant fallback to a 13B optimized model if queue latency > 2s for >2 minutes.

What we need from HeliumHealth by EOD Thu:
- Confirmation on preferred AWS regions (we recommended west prim + east standby).
- Approximated daily batch windows and a sample batch job manifest (you mentioned nightly re-runs).
- Any procurement lead to loop in for reserved capacity quotes.

Internal action items (assigned):
- @rishi_malhotra: please prepare a provisional capacity reservation for us-west-2: 8 baseline nodes, warm reserve 4, burst policy config (min/target/max) and estimated peak token costs. Note netops contact/ports required for cross-region peering.
- @monica_patel: I need a short runbook for rollback (canary -> full) and a checklist for cutover testing with our CS engineers.
- I'll coordinate an intake call with HeliumHealth and our cloud team; proposed slot Fri 9am PST.

Attaching two starter artifacts: helhealth-security-answers.pdf (answers you provided) and draft-pool-topology.png (proposed network layout).

If that sounds good we can lock dates and I’ll get Rishi to simulate cost numbers.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

--
Priya Natarajan
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Dec 2026 09:18:00 -0500
Subject: INTERNAL: HeliumHealth staging reserve + burst sim (please action)

Rishi / Ben — we have tentative signoff from Alicia (see thread). Please treat this as activation prep for a staging pool (do not commit costs to billing until procurement signs).

Rishi: actionables
- Build a provisional reservation in us-west-2 for 8 baseline A100 nodes (quantized 16-bit path) + warm reserve 4 nodes. Provide an expected per-hour token cost and a 30-day burn estimate. Include impact of 2-level autoscale (fast burst up to 24 nodes).
- Confirm whether warm reserve uses preloaded KV caches or just pre-initialized model workers. If we can preload KV caches for the 30B model, cold-starts drop significantly (note: that will add ~30-45% memory overhead).
- Flag any netops prerequisites for east-1 standby peering (IP ranges, routes, peering ACLs).

Ben: actionables
- Draft an ops test plan with rollback gates. Include: canary traffic percentage, SLA fallback triggers, and at least one manual rollback procedure.

Monica: can you draft a short checklist for CS-run cutover with HeliumHealth engineering (5–7 items) and estimate an amount of test traffic we should emulate?

Timing: please get back with numbers/plan by EOD Thu (9 Dec). We’re aiming for a staged activation window the following week (target Mon 13 Dec for initial cutover simulation).

Thanks — Priya

From: Alicia Vega <alicia.vega@heliumhealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Bowers <tom.bowers@heliumhealth.com>, HeliumHealth Procurement <procurement@heliumhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Dec 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial ask — staging region and burst behavior for dedicated pool

Priya — this all looks good to us. Confirming: us-west primary + us-east warm standby, 8 baseline / warm reserve 4 / burst to 24.

Procurement is looped for reserved-capacity quote (procurement@heliumhealth.com). Tom will share a sample batch manifest by EOD today. We will sign the preliminary SOW once we get your cost sim.

One note: our security team asked if you can provide a short note on data residency for staging logs (we keep staging telemetry for 30 days). If you can add that to the activation checklist that’d be helpful.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the Friday call.

Best,
Alicia
